item.title: WAVLINK router perfect CVSS 10 zero day CVE-2026-120345 exploited in wild DNS command injection attacks
item.description:
Network perimeter threat intelligence advisories issued today warn of active wild exploitation targeting wireless routing hardware. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit malformed DNS resolution requests over the public internet to execute arbitrary operating system commands under root administrative privileges.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-120345 with a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, affects WAVLINK WN551X3-A routers running firmware build M51X3_V251020-WO-182e965. The defect resides within the DNS resolution handler function sub_41a430 inside the binary /bin/ioos. Unauthenticated remote threat actors submit crafted data arguments within DNS resolution requests to inject operating system commands directly into system execution subroutines. Threat telemetry confirms public exploit code is actively weaponized by automated scanning botnets targeting exposed SMB edge routers.
Subverting perimeter wireless routing devices undermines network boundary controls across small business and branch office networks. Because edge routers manage local IP routing, DNS resolution, and gateway access control lists, an unauthenticated remote command execution compromise permits adversaries to capture transit traffic, rewrite internal DNS records, and pivot into corporate subnets.
- Isolate WAVLINK WN551X3-A routing hardware from untrusted external interfaces immediately and verify vendor firmware updates. - Restrict remote WAN management and DNS query resolution interfaces to isolated, trusted IP ranges. - Inspect network gateway traffic for anomalous outbound connections or unverified DNS resolution payloads. - Replace unpatchable or end-of-life edge routing hardware with enterprise-grade access control gateways.
Edge network hardware defense demands rigid parameter sanitization and immediate firmware updates to ensure gateway devices remain protected against unauthenticated remote command injection exploits. #CodeDefence #WAVLINK #RouterSecurity #CommandInjection #RCE #ZeroDay #PerimeterSecurity #NetworkSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Google and law enforcement dismantle massive 1.3 million device XCPE Android TV botnet infrastructure
item.description:
Cyber threat infrastructure disclosures published today detail a major international law enforcement action targeting malicious botnet operations. Security teams severed command-and-control channels driving a global network of over one million compromised consumer devices.
The coordinated operation, led by Google Threat Intelligence alongside federal law enforcement agencies, disrupted the XCPE botnet. Threat actors infected over 1.3 million unmanaged Android TV streaming devices globally by exploiting unpatched firmware vulnerabilities and trojanized third-party media applications. The botnet operators weaponized compromised endpoints to conduct high-volume distributed denial-of-service attacks, proxy residential web traffic for fraud campaigns, and deliver secondary malware payloads. Command-and-control domain infrastructures were seized and sinkholed.
Subverting edge internet-of-things devices introduces significant distributed network risk and residential proxy abuse across enterprise networks. When unmanaged streaming devices and smart hardware operate on corporate branch subnets, infected endpoints allow threat actors to anonymize malicious traffic and launch internal reconnaissance sweeps.
- Segment internet-of-things and smart TV streaming hardware onto dedicated, isolated guest network subnets. - Enforce strict egress network filtering to block unauthorized outbound connections originating from unmanaged endpoints. - Deploy automated endpoint detection tools to identify unverified proxy traffic traversing corporate network perimeters. - Audit enterprise network perimeters for unmanaged consumer IoT devices connected to internal production VLANs.
Network infrastructure governance requires strict device isolation and continuous egress traffic monitoring to ensure unmanaged endpoint infections cannot compromise corporate enterprise operations. #CodeDefence #Google #XCPE #Botnet #AndroidTV #IoTSecurity #DDoS #NetworkSecurity #ThreatIntelligence #AppSec

item.title: Trojanized Claude Code VS Code extension on Cursor marketplace exposes developer SSH keys and source code
item.description:
Developer environment security alerts published today detail a supply-chain intrusion vector targeting software engineering workstations. Malicious actors distributed a fake artificial intelligence coding extension to install persistent backdoor access across developer endpoints.
The supply chain incident involved a trojanized extension impersonating Anthropic Claude Code distributed through the Cursor extension marketplace. Threat actors published the malicious extension under a typo-squatted developer identity, remaining active for 11 hours and infecting up to 5,000 developer environments. The embedded malicious payload executed post-install scripts to exfiltrate SSH private keys, cloud infrastructure API tokens, and local environment variables while installing persistent remote shell backdoors.
Subverting integrated development environment extension marketplaces presents severe software supply chain and credential theft risks. Because developer workstations hold elevated access to source code repositories, cloud hosting accounts, and continuous integration pipelines, unmonitored IDE extensions allow threat actors to compromise production software builds and pivot into enterprise cloud infrastructure.
- Audit developer workstation extensions immediately and remove unverified third-party tools installed from external marketplaces. - Force immediate rotation of all SSH private keys, cloud access tokens, and API credentials stored on compromised developer endpoints. - Enforce enterprise-managed extension whitelisting policies within developer IDE environments to block unverified installations. - Monitor developer endpoint process execution trees for unauthorized SSH session spawns or anomalous network connections.
Developer workstation defense demands strict marketplace extension governance and automated secret rotation to ensure software development environments remain protected against supply-chain extension compromises. #CodeDefence #Anthropic #ClaudeCode #Cursor #SupplyChain #DevSecOps #AppSec #EndpointSecurity #IdentitySecurity
